metadata.creator: Supreme Court of the United States
metadata.description:
Case name: Arkansas v. Farm Credit Servs. of Central Ark.

Opinion filed: 1997-06-02

Docket No.: 95-1918

Citations:
• 138 L. Ed. 2d 34
• 117 S. Ct. 1776
• 520 U.S. 821
• 1997 U.S. LEXIS 3395

Case holding summaries:
• "We have interpreted and applied the Tax Injunction Act as a `jurisdictional rule' and a `broad jurisdictional barrier'" (quoting Moe v. Confederated Salish & Kootenai Tribes of Flathead Reservation, 425 U.S. 463, 470, 96 S.Ct. 1634, 48 L.Ed.2d 96 (1976))
• "We have interpreted and applied the Tax Injunction Act as a `jurisdictional rule' and a `broad jurisdictional barrier'" (quoting Moe v. Confederated Salish & Kootenai Tribes of Flathead Reservation, 425 U.S. 463, 470, 96 S.Ct. 1634, 48 L.Ed.2d 96 (1976
• "The [TIA] is grounded in the need of States to administer their fiscal affairs without undue interference from federal courts."
• explaining that the Tax Injunction Actwhich has operative language similar to § 2254(d) ("The district courts shall not enjoin . . ."
• although Production Credit Associations were federal instrumentalities, they could not sue for an injunction against state taxation under the Tax Injunction Act, unless the federal government was a co-plaintiff
• "The States' interest in the integrity of their own processes is of par- ticular moment respecting questions of state taxation."
• noting that it is a “basic principle that statu- tory language is to be enforced according to its terms”
• The restrictions of § 2283 are inapplicable in a suit brought by the National Government
• "It is reasonable, as a prerequisite to by-passing normal state tax collection and litigation channels, that [the instrumentalities] persuade the Attorney General of the United States . . . to join in their claim"
• agreeing with the First Circuit in State Tax Commission that "such joinder [with the United States as co-plaintiff] is necessary before a federal instrumentality can overcome the restrictions" of the Tax Injunction Act
• describing Federal Reserve bank standard as a "flexible test"
• "The exclusiveness of the federal domain is clear . . ."
• barring suit that sought exemption from sales and income taxes
• corporations chartered under federal law claimed exemption from Arkansas sales and income taxation
